items.text: I work in a pedestrian area near the city centre.

steps.title: Look at the two sentences again.
steps.sub: I work in a pedestrian area. · Today I’m working from 7 to 3.
steps.prompt: Which form do we use for a routine — something that is always true?
steps.answer: I work (Present Simple)
steps.why: The Present Simple is for what is usually true; the Present Continuous is for now or around now.

steps.title: Present Simple and Present Continuous
steps.html:
Use it forPresent SimplePresent Continuous
a routineI serve tea every day.—
right now—I’m working from 7 to 3 today.
a factThe market opens at six.—
a change—More people are reading in Hindi these days.
negativeHe doesn’t work alone.He isn’t working today.
questionDo you work alone?What are you doing now?

Present Simple: every day, usually, always, never, on Mondays. Add -s for he / she / it.

Present Continuous: am / is / are + -ing. Use it for this moment, for today, and for a situation that is changing.

Time words help you choose: usually, every day, often → Simple. now, at the moment, today, this week → Continuous.

Some verbs are almost never continuous: know, like, want, need, understand, believe. Say I know the street, not I am knowing the street.

The Present Continuous comes back in Unit 4 for future arrangements: I’m meeting Ana on Friday.

steps.title: Listen to the first interview: Edgar Mueller.
steps.sub: Listen once for the main idea.
steps.prompt: Why does Edgar think 3D pavement art is popular?
options: People meet the art in the street, on their way to work.
It is a great deal cheaper than going to a museum or gallery.
It stays on the ground for many years without being damaged.
steps.answer: People meet the art in the street, on their way to work.
steps.why: “The art happens outside, so people can enjoy the art on their way to work.”

steps.title: Listen again. Choose the correct answer.
steps.prompt: Why does Edgar make such huge paintings?
options: He wants to change how the street looks.
He wants to break a world record every year.
He is paid by the square metre.
steps.answer: He wants to change how the street looks.

steps.title: Listen again. Choose the correct answer.
steps.prompt: What does he want people to do with the paintings?
options: Walk on them and become part of the art.
Photograph them and put them online.
Buy them and take them home.
steps.answer: Walk on them and become part of the art.

steps.title: Listen again. True or False?
steps.prompt: Edgar’s painting Ice Age broke a world record.
steps.answer: True

steps.title: Listen again. True or False?
steps.prompt: Edgar is interested in the way people see the world.
steps.answer: True

steps.title: Listen to the second interview: Laxman Rao.

steps.prompt: What are Laxman’s two jobs?
options: He sells tea and he writes books.

steps.answer: He sells tea and he writes books.
steps.why: He serves tea at a stall in central Delhi and writes novels and plays in Hindi.

steps.title: Listen again. Choose the correct answer.
steps.prompt: How long has he worked at the stall?

steps.title: Listen again. Choose the correct answer.
steps.prompt: Why does he think his luck is changing?

A publisher has bought his novels.
steps.answer: More and more people are reading in Hindi.
steps.why: A change happening now — and he says it with the Present Continuous: “more and more people are reading…”

steps.title: Listen again. Choose the correct answer.
steps.prompt: Who publishes his books?
options: He does — he is writer, publisher and salesman.
steps.answer: He does — he is writer, publisher and salesman.
